speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces. To understand the cause, have you recently started any new medications, particularly sulfonamides or allopurinol?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (likely triggered by captopril, with meloxicam as a potential contributing factor).

The combination of blisters on the forearm, painful oral ulcers, and genital pain in a patient recently started on captopril and recently discontinued meloxicam is highly suggestive of this severe cutaneous adverse reaction. Given the severity and potential for rapid progression, immediate cessation of the offending agents and urgent medical evaluation are required.
